newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open steady, block deals dominate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open steady, block deals dominate.

text.p: Singapore shares held steady in listless trade at mid-morning on Thursday amid concerns over the direction of U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
"Volume is very thin. There is prevailing uncertainty about direction of U.S. interest rates. My sentiment is more negative than positive," a broker with a local brokerage house said.
At 0245 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 3.72 points at 2,186.03. Market volume was light at 27.1 million shares, with losers leading gainers at 92 to 89.
SingTel 100 led the actives with 1.8 million shares on profit-taking by some Singaporeans ahead of September 20.

"Some of the man-in-the-street, mostly the old folks, are selling their SingTel shares so that they realise their profits in October," another dealer said. "However, this selling pressure should ease next week. At S$3, SingTel is a good buy." Malaysia's Metroplex Bhd and Kemayan Corp were also active with 1.5 million and 1.1 million shares traded respectively. Dealers said Metroplex saw a block deal of one million at Singapore $1.64 and Kemayan 750,000 at S$2.01.
Rashid Hussain led the gainers at S$7.10, up 30 cents while Seaview led the losers, shedding 30 cents to S$14.40.
